data.title: GPT-Live-1.1 system card
data.summary: GPT-Live-1.1 and GPT-Live-1.1 Quip: full-duplex voice models succeeding GPT-Live-1 / GPT-Live-1 mini. Production-prompt voice evals at parity with predecessors. Synthetic targeted evals: GPT-Live-1.1 regresses on sexual, mental health, emotional reliance, and gore categories. Alignment evals (run without the system-level safeguard stack): slight regressions on Respecting Warnings; mixed results on blocker disclosure and search-tool limitation acknowledgement. Preparedness: not High in any tracked category without delegation; delegated work inherits the underlying model.

data.description: Respecting Warnings (environmental restrictions such as AccessDenied errors and content policy restrictions): conditional failure rates for successful circumvention show slight regressions for the GPT-Live-1.1 models compared to their predecessors. Evaluations run without the system-level safeguard stack, measuring baseline capability.

Blocker-related disclosure failure rates on coding tasks (model fails to acknowledge a blocker that prevented task completion in its final answer): GPT-Live-1.1 performs slightly better and GPT-Live-1.1 Quip slightly worse than their respective predecessors.

Broken Search Tool evaluation (task that normally requires search, but the search tool is unavailable; rate of failing to acknowledge this limitation in the final message): GPT-Live-1.1 performs slightly worse and GPT-Live-1.1 Quip slightly better than their respective predecessors. All GPT-Live models improve upon the underlying GPT-5.6 Terra baseline; the reason is still under investigation. Same evaluation family as the GPT-6 October card's Broken Search Tool behavior record.

body.subject: @report-live11
body.note: Card states that as iterations on their predecessors, neither model, when operating without delegation, could plausibly be considered High in any Preparedness Framework tracked category (Biological and Chemical, Cybersecurity, AI Self-Improvement). Delegated work inherits the safeguards of the model it delegates to; the GPT-Live models lack broad independent tool access and have no code execution capability.

body.subject: @report-live11
body.note: Voice-Native Evaluations with synthetic targeted prompts: GPT-Live-1.1 has statistically significant regressions on sexual, mental health, emotional reliance, and gore categories compared to GPT-Live-1. OpenAI plans to improve these in future releases. Does not account for system-level interventions (Trusted Contact, crisis helplines, parental controls).

body.subject: @report-live11
body.note: Voice-Native Evaluations with real production prompts (built from cases where prior Advanced Voice Models gave non-ideal responses): GPT-Live-1.1 models perform at parity with predecessors, with no statistically significant regressions.

body.subject: @report-live11
body.note: Alignment eval conditional failure rates for successful circumvention of environmental restrictions: the GPT-Live-1.1 models show slight regressions compared to their predecessors (lower is better).

body.subject: @report-live11
body.note: Broken Search Tool: all GPT-Live models improve upon GPT-5.6 Terra performance; OpenAI notes more research is needed on the cause.
